location.region: Uji and other regions (co-product of sencha/gyokuro processing)

characteristics.roast: None (or light if prepared as roasted hoji-kukicha)

description.short: Light, naturally sweet tea made from stems and stalks, a delightful byproduct of sencha and gyokuro sorting
description.overview: Crafted exclusively from tender stems, petioles, and veins separated during the sorting of premium whole-leaf teas — a remarkable example of zero-waste artisanal Japanese tea production.
description.leaf: Slender pale green and ivory twigs and stalks rather than flat leaf lamina
description.taste: Crisp, naturally sweet, free from bitterness and heavy astringency, remarkably clean
description.processing: Sorting raw aracha after sencha or gyokuro processing → mechanical air and screen separation of stems from leaf flakes → final drying

history.origin: Began as a resourceful way for farming families to enjoy tea without wasting the stems sorted out of high-value commercial leaf consignments.
history.development: A prestigious grade called 'Karigane' (or Shiragiku) made exclusively from shaded gyokuro and tencha stems emerged as an elite culinary delicacy.
history.modern: Prized for its naturally low caffeine content (stems contain far less caffeine than leaf blades) and gentle digestive qualities, making it a soothing daily beverage.
interestingFacts: Despite being composed of sorted 'stems', top-grade Karigane from shaded gyokuro gardens often commands higher prices than ordinary leaf sencha due to extraordinary L-theanine sweetness concentrated in stems.
Its exceptionally low caffeine levels make kukicha a traditional favorite for macrobiotic diets, children, and evening sipping.
